chunks: And in the narration of al-Sakuni:

That three men testified against a man for zina. So Ali, peace be upon him, said: “Where is the fourth?” They said: “He is coming now.” So he, peace be upon him, said: “Administer the hadd punishment to them, for in the hudud there is no delaying for even an hour.”

key_terms.الرَّابِعُ: the required fourth witness in this legal context
key_terms.الزِّنَا: illicit sexual intercourse subject to legal punishment
key_terms.الْحُدُودِ: fixed legal punishments in the Sacred Law
key_terms.نَظَرُ سَاعَةٍ: delay or postponement even for a short time

ai.seo_question: What happens if only three witnesses testify in a zina accusation in Islamic law?
ai.summary: This hadith states that an accusation of zina is not established by the testimony of only three witnesses. Imam Ali عليه السلام ordered punishment for the accusers, indicating the strict evidentiary standard in hudud cases and the impermissibility of delaying enforcement once the legal deficiency was clear.

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications: Hadith.5021 - In the narration from Al-Sakuni,

it is reported that three individuals testified against a man for committing adultery.
Imam Ali ibn Abi Talib (as) asked: "Where is the fourth witness?"
They replied: "He is coming now."
Imam Ali ibn Abi Talib (as) then said: "Administer the punishment to them, for there is no delay in enforcing legal punishments."
